title: Erasure of Unaligned Attributes from Neural Representations
findings: Removing religious bias from model representations is challenging and highly dependent on the specific model. The paper found that religion (along with race) was more difficult to debias in BERT compared to gender. The proposed debiasing methods showed mixed results for religion; in some cases, they reduced stereotypical scores, but in others, the bias score increased, indicating that the debiasing was not consistently effective across all models and setups.

measurement_description: Detection of stereotypical bias related to religion. The benchmarks, such as CrowS-Pairs and StereoSet, measure how often a language model prefers a stereotypical sentence or completion over a non-stereotypical one. The SEAT benchmark measures the association between religious attribute words and target words.
